title: What DSPM integrations do: cloud storage, ITSM, ChatOps and Amazon Security Lake export

prose.label: Limits.
prose.text: Slack and Jira limits beyond those above are not covered {{gap:limits-and-alert-rules}}. The alert rules that send to these integrations are in [[dspm.alerts:rule-channel-itsm]] and [[dspm.alerts:rule-channel-storage-chatops]].

checks.do: Whether alert notification rules are associated with an integration that still shows Pending, since the pages say data is sent only after they are.
Whether the Amazon S3 bucket default encryption is SSE-S3, since selecting SSE-KMS makes the connection fail.

purpose-and-tools.statement: DSPM integrations share findings (alerts) with other tools: cloud storage (Amazon S3, Azure Blob Storage, Amazon Security Lake), ITSM (Jira, ServiceNow) and ChatOps (Slack).

quotes: Integrations allow DSPM to share findings (alerts) with other tools in your organization's ecosystem.
- Cloud storage services: Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3), Azure Blob Storage, and Amazon Security Lake
- ITSM tools: Jira and ServiceNow
- ChatOps tools: Slack

status-values.statement: On the Integrations page the Status column, listed for Cloud Storage, ITSM and ChatOps (Slack) integrations, shows Success, Failed, Paused or Pending for the previous data transfer, with the failure reason on hover.

evidence.after: View the list of cloud storage integrations. For each integration, you can see:
quotes: Status: The outcome (Success, Failed, Paused, or Pending) of the previous data transfer. For failed status, hover over the label to see the reason for failure.

evidence.after: View the list of ITSM integrations. For each ITSM integration, you can see:
quotes: Status: The outcome (Success, Failed, Paused, or Pending) of the previous data transfer. For failed status, hover over the label to see the reason for failure.

evidence.after: View the list of Slack integrations. For each integration, you can see:
quotes: Status: The outcome (Success, Failed, Paused, or Pending) of the previous data transfer. For failed status, hover over the label to see the reason for failure.

data-transfer-toggle.statement: Data transfer is enabled by default on a cloud storage integration; disabling it pauses transfer without deleting the integration, and a transfer in progress completes first.

quotes: By default, the data transfer is enabled. If you want to pause the transfer without deleting the integration, click the toggle to disable the data transfer. If any data transfer is in progress, the activity is completed and then the data transfer is disabled.

admin-role.statement: Only users with the administrator role can configure cloud storage integrations.

quotes: Only users with the administrator role can configure cloud storage integrations.

edit-retest.statement: After changing values in an integration, the connection must be tested again.

quotes: If you change the values, you must test the connection again.

delete-blocked-by-alert-rules.statement: An integration associated with alert rules cannot be deleted; the alert rules must first be moved to another integration, and the Delete button stays disabled until then.

quotes: You cannot delete an integration if it is associated with alert rules. You must first move the alert rules to another integration. Until then, the Delete button is disabled.

initial-pending.statement: A new Amazon S3 integration shows Pending until alert notification rules are associated with it and DSPM sends data logs, after which the status changes to Success.

quotes: The initial status is shown as Pending because data is not yet sent to the Amazon S3 bucket.
You must first configure and associate the alert notification rules with this integration for DSPM to be able to send the data logs.
After DSPM sends the data logs to the Amazon S3 Bucket, then the status changes to Success.

s3-sse-kms-fails.statement: For the Amazon S3 integration the bucket default encryption must be Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3); selecting AWS KMS (SSE-KMS) makes the connection fail.

quotes: Select Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3) as the encryption key type for the connection to be successful and eventually for seamless data transfer.
If you select AWS Key Management Service (SSE-KMS), then the connection fails.

s3-bucket-policy.statement: The Amazon S3 integration gives DSPM access through a bucket policy copied from the Admin Console and pasted into the bucket in AWS, and takes the bucket Folder Location.

quotes: Copy the S3 Bucket policy: Click the icon to copy the S3 Bucket policy.
The policy authorizes DSPM to access the S3 bucket.
You need to paste this policy in the AWS Management Console.
enter the Folder Location of the bucket.

blob-connection-string.statement: The Azure Blob Storage integration uses a storage account connection string; the Container Location is optional, but a folder must first be created in Blob Storage before entering its name.

quotes: Azure Storage Account Connection String: Paste the connection string you copied from the Azure portal.
(Optional) Container Location: Enter the location of the storage container. It is mandatory to first create a folder in your Azure Blob Storage and then add the name.

blob-purpose.statement: The Azure Blob Storage integration sends alert data logs to Blob Storage containers for analysis by third-party SIEM or ITSM tools.

quotes: This integration enables DSPM to send the alert data logs of your cloud resources to the Azure Blob Storage containers for storage and data analysis by third-party SIEM or ITSM tools.

itsm-lifecycle.statement: Depending on configuration, DSPM creates ITSM tickets when a misconfiguration or vulnerability is first detected, updates them as scans continue, and closes them when a posture change or manual remediation resolves the issue.

quotes: Automatic Creation: DSPM automatically creates a ticket when a cloud resource misconfiguration or vulnerability is first detected.
Real-Time Updates: Tickets are updated with the latest context and status changes as DSPM continuously scans your environment.
Automatic Closure: When a posture change or manual remediation resolves the underlying security issue, DSPM automatically closes the associated ticket in your ITSM tool
Depending on your configuration, DSPM APIs dynamically manage the life cycle of these tickets:

jira-oauth.statement: Jira integration needs an OAuth 2.0 (3LO) app in the Atlassian Developer console with Jira API scopes and the Admin Console application URL as Callback URL; its Client ID and Client Secret are entered in DSPM, and Jira cloud versions are supported, provided there is support for the required authentication mechanism and APIs to create a Jira task.

quotes: You must first complete the OAuth configuration before integrating DSPM with Jira.
Sign in to the Atlassian Developer console.
Select the scope for the required Jira features that you want to use for this integration.
Under Create a New OAuth 2.0 (3LO) integration, enter a name for the application.
For Callback URL, paste the application URL you copied from the Zscaler Admin Console.
Copy the Client ID and Client Secret. You need to use these values while adding the Jira integration in the Zscaler Admin Console.
DSPM can be integrated with Jira cloud versions, provided there is support for the required authentication mechanism and APIs to create a Jira task.

servicenow-fields.statement: The ServiceNow integration needs an online ServiceNow instance and takes a hostname, username and password, with a Test Connection step.

quotes: Ensure that your ServiceNow instance is online.
ServiceNow Hostname: Enter the ServiceNow hostname.
ServiceNow Username: Enter the username for ServiceNow.
ServiceNow Password: Enter the password for ServiceNow.
Test Connection: Click to verify the connection between DSPM and ServiceNow.

slack-webhook-limits.statement: The Slack integration uses an incoming webhook, only one webhook per Slack channel, and up to 10 channels per integration.

quotes: Incoming webhooks are used to post messages from the DSPM app to Slack.
You can add only one Webhook per Slack channel.
DSPM allows you to add 10 channels per integration. You can configure another integration to add more channels.

data-flow-needs-alert-rules.statement: For Slack, data is sent only once alert notification rules are configured and associated with the integration.

quotes: you must configure and associate the alert notification rules with this integration for DSPM to be able to send the data logs.

slack-channel-count-column.statement: The Slack integrations list shows Channels as the number of channels added for sending notifications.

quotes: Channels: The number of channels that are added for sending notifications.

overview-ocsf-parquet.statement: Amazon Security Lake uses OCSF for alert information and requires Parquet for stored alerts; DSPM exports alerts to a pre-configured S3 bucket.

quotes: Amazon Security Lake uses the Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF) as the selected format for the alert information and requires the Parquet file format for the stored alerts.
export and store the alert data in a dedicated Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3) bucket that is pre-configured as part of the Amazon Security Lake setup.

custom-source.statement: Zscaler is set up as a custom source in Security Lake using the Security_Finding event class, in the region where the AWS console is connected; the source name determines the S3 path.

quotes: Event class: Make sure you use the Security_Finding event class.
The custom source is created in the region where the AWS console is connected.
This name determines the path in the S3 bucket to which the alert data is written.

custom-source-ids.statement: The custom source takes the account ID and external ID copied from the Cloud Storage page in the Admin Console, which identify DSPM as the source writing to the data lake.

quotes: External ID: Enter the external ID that you copied from the Cloud Storage page in the Zscaler Admin Console.
Account ID: Enter the account ID that you copied from the Cloud Storage page in the Zscaler Admin Console.
The AWS Account ID and External ID are identifiers of the custom source (DSPM) that writes logs and events to the data lake.

test-connection-checks-bucket.statement: The Security Lake Test Connection validates that the S3 bucket exists.

quotes: The test connection validates that the S3 bucket exists.

partitioning.statement: Files are posted when they reach 256 MB or after 5 minutes, under region=<awsregion>/accountid=<cloudaccountid>/eventDay=<YYYYMMDD> in the custom source root path.

quotes: A new file is generated and posted whenever the file size reaches 256 MB or after 5 minutes.
The folder structure is: region=<awsregion>/accountid=<cloudaccountid>/eventDay=<YYYYMMDD>.
The files are stored under the root path created for the custom source.

ocsf-static-values.statement: Alerts are written with static OCSF values category_uid 2, class_uid 2001, metadata.product.name dspm and metadata.version 2.2.

quotes: | category_uid |  | 2 |
| class_uid |  | 2001 |
| metadata.product.name |  | dspm |
| metadata.version |  | 2.2 |

ocsf-field-map.statement: OCSF fields map from DSPM alert fields: severity from risk, finding.uid from alert_id, finding.title from policy_name, and time from csp_event_timestamp.

quotes: | severity | risk |  |
| finding.uid | alert_id |  |
| finding.title | policy_name |  |
| time | csp_event_timestamp |  |

ocsf-status-map.statement: OCSF activity maps from the DSPM alert_status field and status_detail from alert_status_description.

quotes: | activity | alert_status |  |
| status_detail | alert_status_description |  |

troubleshoot-glue-crawler.statement: If alert data is in the Security Lake bucket but the Glue Crawler fails to parse it, the cause is typically a custom source created with the wrong event class; it must use the Security Finding event class.

quotes: This issue typically occurs when the custom source that is created for the integration is using the wrong event class. Make sure you create the custom source with the Security Finding event class.

troubleshoot-failed-status.statement: A Failed status on the Security Lake integration indicates DSPM lacks permission to access the Amazon Security Lake S3 bucket; the page tells readers to apply the required policy granting DSPM access.

quotes: This indicates that DSPM does not have the permission to access the Amazon Security Lake S3 bucket.
make sure you have applied the required policy to grant DSPM access to the S3 bucket.

troubleshoot-not-exported.statement: If new alerts appear in the Admin Console but are not exported to Security Lake, the alert rule notification configuration and the alert rule scope should be checked.

quotes: Make sure you've configured the alert rule notification and check the scope of the alert rule.

limits-and-alert-rules.title: Which Slack and Jira limits apply
limits-and-alert-rules.detail: The integration pages state one webhook per Slack channel and 10 channels per integration, and give read:jira-work only as an example scope. Alert rules sending to Cloud Storage, ITSM and ChatOps are covered by dspm.alerts claims rule-channel-itsm and rule-channel-storage-chatops.

security-lake-failed-policy.title: Which policy the Security Lake Failed-status resolution means
security-lake-failed-policy.detail: The troubleshooting row says to apply 'the required policy' to grant DSPM access to the S3 bucket, but the Security Lake setup steps grant access through the custom source's IAM role and external ID and never define a policy; do not apply the s3-bucket-policy steps here without confirming.

ocsf-mapping-incomplete.title: What the remaining Security Lake OCSF mapping rows hold
ocsf-mapping-incomplete.detail: The mapping table has rows with empty static values and NA attack fields, and finding.desc and resources.0.details point to files not included on the page.
